name: Susan Carol Holland
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Susan Carol Holland is the chair of the board of Milan-based Amplifon, the world's largest retailer of hearing aids.
Amplifon was founded in 1950 by her father, British-born Algernon Charles Holland, to provide hearing care for people injured in World War II.
Her father served in the British Special Operations Executive during the war, receiving the honor of Member of the Order of the British Empire.
Amplifon developed digital hearing aids in the 1990s and entered the North American market with the acquisition of Miracle-Ear in 1999.
Algernon died in 2001, the same year Amplifon went public on the Italian Stock Exchange; Susan took over as chair in 2011.

name: Mehmet Hattat
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2011-2018); Hurun Global (2014-2021)
forbes_bio: Mehmet Hattat's companies operate in manufacturing, mining, energy and real estate.
At a complex of 11 factories, Hattat make parts and components for autos, commercial vehicles and companies in the aviation and defense industries.
Hattat makes Massey Ferguson and Ferrari tractors for the foreign market, as well as  tractors bearing the Hattat brand name.
Hattat is developing a project (hotel, shopping center, conference center and office space) on land he owns in the affluent Maslak area of Istanbul.
He plans on using coal from a mine he owns in Northern Turkey to fuel a nearby 1320 MW thermal power plant, in which he is an investor.
forbes_facts: He owns two vases from the Napoleonic era bearing the initials of Napoleon and his wife, Josephine.

name: Chang Kuo-Cheng
forbes_bio: Chang Kuo-Cheng is the third son of shipping tycoon Chang Yung Fa, who died in 2016 at the age of 88.
In 1968 Yung Fa founded Evergreen Marine, now one of the world's largest transportation companies.
Brothers Kuo-Hua, Kuo-Ming and Kuo-Cheng also inherited stakes in EVA Airways and hotels in Taiwan, mainland China, Paris and Bangkok.

name: Amelie Voigt Trejes
forbes_bio: Amelie Voigt Trejes, one of the world's youngest billionaires, is one of the largest individual shareholders of WEG, the largest manufacturer of electrical motors in Latin America.
The company was cofounded by her grandfather Werner Ricardo Voigt along with late billionaires Eggon Joao da Silva and Geraldo Werninghaus.
A publicly-traded multinational with factories in over ten countries, WEG has annual revenue of approximately $7 billion.
Amelie does not hold a board seat or any executive position at WEG; her twin brothers are also major shareholders.
forbes_facts: Voigt Trejes became the world's youngest billionaire in 2026, deposing German pharmaceutical heir, Johannes von Baumbach.

name: Wang Jiufang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2010-2018); Hurun China (2006-2007)
forbes_bio: Wang Jiufang is the chairman of Ningbo-based developer Rongan Property, a real estate concern.
He shares his fortune with son Wang Congwei, a Rongan director and general manager.

name: Tan Yu Wei
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2022-2025)
forbes_bio: Tan Yu Wei gets his wealth from his stake in Mr. D.I.Y, a home improvement retail chain, which his older brother, Tan Yu Yeh founded in 2005.
Tan Yu Wei was a director at De Little Chinatown, a wholesaler of Chinese products, until 2011 when he joined D.I.Y.
The company was listed on the Malaysian stock exchange in October 2020.
Mr. D.I.Y has 835 stores in Malaysia and six stores in Brunei.
